reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown distinguish Acts 9:7's bare hearing of a voice-sound from Acts 22:9's failure to catch the articulate words spoken only to Saul.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg presses the flat contradiction: Acts says the men heard the voice, but Paul's own retelling denies it.

quotes.text: The author of Acts says that his companions heard a voice. Is this true? Paul: “They that were with me ... heard not the voice” (Acts xxii, 9).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on Acts 9:7 and 22:9.

sides.snippet: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.
sides.verseText: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.

sides.snippet: Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn't understand the voice of him who spoke to me.
